summary: LLM agents across model families systematically lose value against the Bayesian reference solver through premature commitments, susceptibility to framed telemetry, and suboptimal active-probing decisions. Agents frequently execute irreversible accusations when suspect uncertainty remains high (between 30% and 60%), throwing away substantial expected value compared to waiting for pending canaries or feed delay windows. They also fall victim to the environment's deceptive decoys and framed after-hours logs, directing accusations at innocent employees and incurring catastrophic -1.0 penalties. Finally, agents squander company value by planting canaries with tiny recipient pools that careful moles avoid, imposing costly access restrictions prematurely, and exhausting daily action limits with malformed or redundant tool calls.

modes.name: Premature Accusation on Sub-Threshold Posterior
modes.description: The agent terminates the episode by accusing a suspect when posterior certainty is still moderate (typically 30% to 60%), rather than waiting for pending canaries, delayed leak feeds, or subsequent document distributions. Even when the target happens to be the true mole, rushing the accusation incurs severe regret because the risk-adjusted expected value of gathering another round of evidence strongly exceeds the marginal cost of waiting.
modes.mechanism: The agent confuses a local likelihood lead or small interview/access-log advantage with definitive certainty, failing to calculate the expected value of waiting for pending canary reports or delay resolution.
modes.solver_would: Wait for pending canaries to surface in the leak feed or plant an orthogonal separating canary, committing to an accusation only when posterior confidence is high enough that the expected gain exceeds the cost of delay.

comparison.cross_family_finding: The single most decisive divergence between the model families is that Gemini models (especially Gemini 4 Carbon) actively gather Bayesian evidence through high-volume staff interviews (~50 interviews per episode) and structured 3-variant canaries, achieving >93% accuracy and rarely accusing falsely, whereas GPT and Grok models almost entirely forgo interviews (2 to 11 per episode) and instead rely heavily on punitive access restrictions and premature accusations on sub-threshold beliefs (<0.60 posterior); however, this comparison is qualified by differing sample sizes and the fact that Gemini was evaluated on tier v1.4 (40 employees, delayed feedback) while GPT and Grok ran primarily on v1.2 and v1.3 (20-30 employees, immediate V drop feedback in v1.2).
comparison.caveats: Comparisons must account for version differences: v1.2 exposed same-day V degradation upon leaks providing an immediate feedback channel, whereas v1.3 and v1.4 masked un-surfaced leak damage. Furthermore, v1.4 increased employee count to 40 on hard tier, altering canary dilution math. Sample sizes also vary widely from 10 episodes in Gemini 3.5 Flash, GPT-5.5 Codex v1.2, GPT-5.6-sol, and Grok, to 40 episodes in GPT-5.5 inproc v1.2.

cohorts.behaviour: Gemini 3.5 Flash plays aggressively with canaries but frequently configures 3-recipient canaries across the 40-person company, which under careful-mole dynamics carry near-zero probability of selection and incur heavy uninformative-canary regret. It conducts zero employee interviews and never uses access restrictions, relying purely on access logs and canary intersections. Although it achieved 100% accuracy in the sample, it occasionally rushes accusations at sub-threshold posteriors with high regret penalties.
